name: vue-why-render
description: See which Vue components re-render — and why. Names the exact prop, ref or store key behind every render.

paragraphs: Other tools flash a border around a component that just updated. That is enough to notice a problem, but not to fix it — you are still left asking what actually changed? vue-why-render answers that: it names the exact reactive dependency that triggered the render.
In React you have to guess this by diffing props. Vue hands you the reason itself, through the renderTriggered hook — this package is built around it.
features: The reason, not just the fact: the name of the prop, ref, store key or array index, plus the old and new value.
A dedicated "new reference, same value" verdict — by far the most common source of wasted renders.
Overlay: a border around the re-rendered component, coloured from green to red by frequency.
Panel: top by render count, top by time, a component tree with per-subtree totals, and an event feed.
Jump to your editor: clicking a row opens the SFC in your IDE through the dev server.

whatItDoes.text: Other tools flash a border around a component that just updated. That is enough to notice a problem, but not to fix it — you are still left asking what actually changed? vue-why-render answers that: it names the exact reactive dependency that triggered the render.

requirements.text: Nothing to configure — it appears when DevTools is open, and costs nothing when it is not.
